[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (8) If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a) the claimant has had notice in accordance with this rule to pay the trial fee;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) the claimant has applied to have the trial fee remitted in whole or part;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (c) remission is refused or only part remission of the trial fee is granted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (d) following the decision on remission, the claimant has had notice in accordance with this rule to pay the full trial fee or balance of it; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (e) the full trial fee or balance of it (as appropriate) has not been paid on or before the revised trial fee payment date,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] the claim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court, and, unless the court orders otherwise, the claimant will be liable for the defendant’s costs in accordance with rule 44.9(1). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (Rule 44.9 provides for the basis of assessment where a right to costs arises under this rule and contains provisions about when a costs order is deemed to have been made and applying for an order under section 194(3) of the Legal Services Act 2007 4 .)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (9) If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a) a claimant applies to have the claim reinstated; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) the court grants relief,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] the relief must be conditional on the claimant either paying the trial fee or filing evidence of full or part remission of that fee within the period specified in paragraph (10). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (10) The period referred to in paragraph (9) is—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (a) if the order granting relief is made at a hearing at which the claimant is present or represented, 2 days from the date of the order;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (b) in any other case, 7 days from the date of service of the order on the claimant. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A1] (11) If a fee is not paid for a claim where there is also a counterclaim, the counterclaim will still stand. ## Sanctions for non-payment of certain fees by the defendant

## 3.7A

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (1) Except where rule 3.7AA applies, this rule applies to fees payable by the defendant where—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (a) a defendant files a counterclaim without –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (i) payment of the fee specified by the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008 5 (Fees Order 2008); or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (ii) making an application for full or part remission of the fee; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (b) the proceedings continue on the counterclaim alone and –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (i) omitted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (ii) omitted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (iii) omitted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (iv) the fee payable for a hearing specified by the Fees Order 2008 is not paid. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (2) The court will serve a notice on the defendant requiring payment of the fee specified in the Fees Order 2008 if, at the time the fee is due, the defendant has not paid it or made an application for full or part remission. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (3) The notice will specify the date by which the defendant must pay the fee. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (4) If the defendant does not –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (a) pay the fee; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (b) make an application for full or part remission of the fee, by the date specified in the notice, the counterclaim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (5) Where an application for –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (a) full or part remission of a fee is refused, the court will serve notice on the defendant requiring payment of the full fee by the date specified in the notice; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (b) part remission of a fee is granted, the court will serve notice on the defendant requiring payment of the balance of the fee by the date specified in the notice. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (6) If the defendant does not pay the fee by the date specified in the notice, the counterclaim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (7) If –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (a) the defendant applies to have the counterclaim reinstated; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (b) the court grants relief, the relief will be conditional on the defendant either paying the fee or filing evidence of full or part remission of the fee within the period specified in paragraph (8). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (8) The period referred to in paragraph (7) is –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (a) if the order granting relief is made at a hearing at which the defendant is present or represented, 2 days from the date of the order;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7A] (b) in any other case, 7 days from the date of service of the order on the defendant. ## 3.7AA

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (1) This rule applies in relation to trial fees where that fee is to be paid by the defendant and the court notifies the defendant in writing of the trial date. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (Definitions contained in rule 3.7A1(1) apply to this rule also.)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (2) When the court notifies the parties in writing of the trial date, the court must also send a fee notice to the defendant. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (3) The fee notice may be contained in the same document as the notice of trial date, or may be a separate document. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (4) Where an application for full or part remission of a trial fee is refused, when the court sends written notice to the defendant of the refusal, the court must also notify the defendant in writing—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (a) that the defendant is required to pay the full trial fee by the revised trial fee payment date; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (b) of the consequences of non-payment of the trial fee. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (5) Where part remission of a fee is granted, when the court sends written notice to the defendant of the part remission, the court must also notify the defendant in writing—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (a) that the defendant is required to pay the balance of the trial fee by the revised trial fee payment date; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (b) of the consequences of non-payment of the balance. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (6) If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (a) the defendant has had notice in accordance with this rule to pay the trial fee;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (b) the defendant has not applied to have the trial fee remitted in whole or part; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (c) the trial fee has not been paid on or before the trial fee payment date,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] the counterclaim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (7) If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (a) the defendant has had notice in accordance with this rule to pay the trial fee;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (b) the defendant has applied to have the trial fee remitted in whole or part;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (c) remission is refused or only part remission of the trial fee is granted;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (d) following the decision on remission, the defendant has had notice in accordance with this rule to pay the full trial fee or balance of it; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (e) the full trial fee or balance of it (as appropriate) has not been paid on or before the revised trial fee payment date,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] the counterclaim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (8) If—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (a) a defendant applies to have the counterclaim reinstated; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (b) the court grants relief,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] the relief will be conditional on the defendant either paying the trial fee or filing evidence of full or part remission of the fee within the period specified in paragraph (9). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (9) The period referred to in paragraph (8) is—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (a) if the order granting relief is made at a hearing at which the defendant is present or represented, 2 days from the date of the order;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7AA] (b) in any other case, 7 days from the date of service of the order on the defendant. ## Sanctions for dishonouring cheque

## 3.7B

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (1) This rule applies where any fee is paid by cheque and that cheque is subsequently dishonoured. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (2) The court will serve a notice on the paying party requiring payment of the fee which will specify the date by which the fee must be paid. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (3) If the fee is not paid by the date specified in the notice –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (a) where the fee is payable by the claimant, the claim will automatically be struck out without further order of the court;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (b) where the fee is payable by the defendant, the defence will automatically be struck out without further order of the court,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] and the paying party shall be liable for the costs which any other party has incurred unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (Rule 44.9 provides for the basis of assessment where a right to costs arises under this rule)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (4) If –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (a) the paying party applies to have the claim or defence reinstated; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (b) the court grants relief,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] the relief shall be conditional on that party paying the fee within the period specified in paragraph (5). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (5) The period referred to in paragraph (4) is –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (a) if the order granting relief is made at a hearing at which the paying party is present or represented, 2 days from the date of the order;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (b) in any other case, 7 days from the date of service of the order on the paying party. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.7B] (6) For the purposes of this rule, ‘claimant’ includes a claimant in a counterclaim or other additional claim and ‘claim form’ includes a counterclaim or other additional claim. ## Sanctions have effect unless defaulting party obtains relief

## 3.8

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (1) Where a party has failed to comply with a rule, practice direction or court order, any sanction for failure to comply imposed by the rule, practice direction or court order has effect unless the party in default applies for and obtains relief from the sanction. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (Rule 3.9 sets out the circumstances which the court will consider on an application to grant relief from a sanction)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (2) Where the sanction is the payment of costs, the party in default may only obtain relief by appealing against the order for costs. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (3) Where a rule, practice direction or court order –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (a) requires a party to do something within a specified time, and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (b) specifies the consequence of failure to comply,

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] the time for doing the act in question may not be extended by agreement between the parties except as provided in paragraph (4). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.8] (4) In the circumstances referred to in paragraph (3) and unless the court orders otherwise, the time for doing the act in question may be extended by prior written agreement of the parties for up to a maximum of 28 days, provided always that any such extension does not put at risk any hearing date. ## Relief from sanctions

## 3.9

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.9] (1) On an application for relief from any sanction imposed for a failure to comply with any rule, practice direction or court order, the court will consider all the circumstances of the case, so as to enable it to deal justly with the application, including the need –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.9] (a) for litigation to be conducted efficiently and at proportionate cost; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.9] (b) to enforce compliance with rules, practice directions and orders. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.9] (2) An application for relief must be supported by evidence. ## General power of the court to rectify matters where there has been an error of procedure

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > General power of the court to rectify matters where there has been an error of procedure] 3.10 Where there has been an error of procedure such as a failure to comply with a rule or practice direction –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > General power of the court to rectify matters where there has been an error of procedure] (a) the error does not invalidate any step taken in the proceedings unless the court so orders; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > General power of the court to rectify matters where there has been an error of procedure] (b) the court may make an order to remedy the error. ## Orders restraining civil proceedings

## 3.11

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.11] (1) A “civil proceedings order” and an “all proceedings order” under section 42(1A) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 shall include provision for applying to begin, continue or make any application in any civil proceedings. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.11] (2) A practice direction may set out –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.11] (a) the circumstances in which the court has the power to make a civil restraint order against a party to proceedings;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.11] (b) the procedure where a party applies for a civil restraint order against another party; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.11] (c) the consequences of the court making a civil restraint order. ## II COSTS MANAGEMENT

## Application of this Section and the purpose of costs management

## 3.12

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.12] (1) This Section and Practice Direction 3D apply to all Part 7 multi-track cases, except—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.12] (a) where the claim is commenced on or after 22nd April 2014 and the amount of money claimed as stated on the claim form is £10 million or more; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.12] (b) where the claim is commenced on or after 22nd April 2014 and is for a monetary claim which is not quantified or not fully quantified or is for a non-monetary claim and in any such case the claim form contains a statement that the claim is valued at £10 million or more; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.12] (c) where in proceedings commenced on or after 6th April 2016 a claim is made by or on behalf of a person under the age of 18 (a child) (and on a child reaching majority this exception will continue to apply unless the court otherwise orders); or (d) where the proceeding are the subject of fixed costs or scale costs; or (e) the court otherwise orders. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.12] (1A) This Section and Practice Direction 3D will apply to any other proceedings (including applications) where the court so orders. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.12] (2) The purpose of costs management is that the court should manage both the steps to be taken and the costs to be incurred by the parties to any proceedings (or variation costs as provided in rule 3.15A) so as to further the overriding objective. ## Filing and exchanging budgets and budget discussion reports

## 3.13

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (1) Unless the court otherwise orders, all parties except litigants in person must file and exchange budgets—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (a) where the stated value of the claim on the claim form is less than £50,000, with their directions questionnaires; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (b) in any other case, not later than 21 days before the first case management conference. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (2) In the event that a party files and exchanges a budget under paragraph (1), all other parties, not being litigants in person, must file an agreed budget discussion report no later than 7 days before the first case management conference. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (3) The court—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (a) may, on its own initiative or on application, order the parties to file and exchange costs budgets in a case where the parties are not otherwise required by this Section to do so;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (b) shall (other than in an exceptional case) make an order to file and exchange costs budgets if all parties consent to an application for such an order. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (4) The court may, in a substantial case, direct that budgets are to be limited in the first instance to part only of the proceedings and extended later to cover the whole proceedings. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (5) Every budget must be dated and verified by a statement of truth signed by a senior legal representative of the party. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.13] (6) Even though a litigant in person is not required to prepare a budget, each other party (other than a litigant in person) must provide the litigant in person with a copy of that party’s budget. ## Failure to file a budget

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Failure to file a budget] 3.14 Unless the court otherwise orders, any party which fails to file a budget despite being required to do so will be treated as having filed a budget comprising only the applicable court fees. ## Costs management orders

## 3.15

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (1) In addition to exercising its other powers, the court may manage the costs to be incurred (the budgeted costs) by any party in any proceedings. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (2) The court may at any time make a ‘costs management order’. Where costs budgets have been filed and exchanged the court will make a costs management order unless it is satisfied that the litigation can be conducted justly and at proportionate cost in accordance with the overriding objective without such an order being made. By a costs management order the court will—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (a) record the extent to which the budgeted costs are agreed between the parties;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (b) in respect of the budgeted costs which are not agreed, record the court’s approval after making appropriate revisions;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (c) record the extent (if any) to which incurred costs are agreed. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (3) If a costs management order has been made, the court will thereafter control the parties’ budgets in respect of recoverable costs. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (4) Whether or not the court makes a costs management order, it may record on the face of any case management order any comments it has about the incurred costs which are to be taken into account in any subsequent assessment proceedings. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (5) Save in exceptional circumstances—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (a )the recoverable costs of initially completing Precedent H (the form to be used for a costs budget) shall not exceed the higher of—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (i) £1,000; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (ii) 1% of the total of the incurred costs (as agreed or allowed on assessment) and the budgeted costs (agreed or approved); and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (b) all other recoverable costs of the budgeting and costs management process shall not exceed 2% of the total of the incurred costs (as agreed or allowed on assessment) and the budgeted (agreed or approved) costs. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (Precedent H is annexed to Practice Direction 3D.)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (6) The court may set a timetable or give other directions for future reviews of budgets. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (7) After a party’s budgeted costs have been approved or agreed, the party must re-file and re-serve the budget—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (a) in the form approved or agreed with re-cast figures; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (b) annexed to the order approving the budgeted costs or recording the parties’ agreement. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15] (8) A costs management order concerns the totals allowed for each phase of the budget, and while the underlying detail in the budget for each phase used by the party to calculate the totals claimed is provided for reference purposes to assist the court in fixing a budget, it is not the role of the court in the costs management hearing to fix or approve the hourly rates claimed in the budget. ## Revision and variation of costs budgets on account of significant developments (“variation costs”)

## 3.15A . [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (1) A party (“the revising party”) must revise its budgeted costs upwards or downwards if significant developments in the litigation warrant such revisions. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (2) Any budgets revised in accordance with paragraph (1) must be submitted promptly by the revising party to the other parties for agreement, and subsequently to the court, in accordance with paragraphs (3) to (5). [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (3) The revising party must—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (a) serve particulars of the variation proposed on every other party, using the form prescribed by Practice Direction 3D;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (b) confine the particulars to the additional costs occasioned by the significant development; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (c) certify, in the form prescribed by Practice Direction 3D, that the additional costs are not included in any previous budgeted costs or variation. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (4) The revising party must submit the particulars of variation promptly to the court, together with the last approved or agreed budget, and with an explanation of the points of difference if they have not been agreed. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (5) The court may approve, vary or disallow the proposed variations, having regard to any significant developments which have occurred since the date when the previous budget was approved or agreed, or may list a further costs management hearing. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.15A .] (6) Where the court makes an order for variation, it may vary the budget for costs related to that variation which have been incurred prior to the order for variation but after the costs management order. ## Costs management conferences

## 3.16

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.16] (1) Any hearing which is convened solely for the purpose of costs management (for example, to approve a revised budget) is referred to as a ‘costs management conference’. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.16] (2) Where practicable, costs management conferences should be conducted by telephone or in writing. ## Court to have regard to budgets and to take account of costs

## 3.17

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.17] (1) When making any case management decision, the court will have regard to any available budgets of the parties and will take into account the costs involved in each procedural step. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.17] (2) Paragraph (1) applies whether or not the court has made a costs management order. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.17] (3) Subject to rule 3.15A, the court—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.17] (a) may not approve costs incurred up to and including the date of any costs management hearing; but

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.17] (b) may record its comments on those costs and take those costs into account when considering the reasonableness and proportionality of all budgeted costs. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.17] (4) If an interim application is made but is not included in a budget, the court may, if it considers it reasonable not to have included the application in the budget, treat the costs of such interim application as additional to the approved budgets. ## Assessing costs on the standard basis where a costs management order has been made

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Assessing costs on the standard basis where a costs management order has been made] 3.18 In any case where a costs management order has been made, when assessing costs on the standard basis, the court will –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Assessing costs on the standard basis where a costs management order has been made] (a) have regard to the receiving party’s last approved or agreed budgeted costs for each phase of the proceedings;

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Assessing costs on the standard basis where a costs management order has been made] (b) not depart from such approved or agreed budgeted costs unless satisfied that there is good reason to do so; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Assessing costs on the standard basis where a costs management order has been made] (c) take into account any comments made pursuant to rule 3.17(3) and recorded on the face of the order. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > Assessing costs on the standard basis where a costs management order has been made] (Attention is drawn to rules 44.3(2)(a) and 44.3(5), which concern proportionality of costs.)

## III COSTS CAPPING

## Costs capping orders – General

## 3.19

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (1) For the purposes of this Section—

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (a) ‘costs capping order’ means an order limiting the amount of future costs (including disbursements) which a party may recover pursuant to an order for costs subsequently made; and

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (b) ‘future costs’ means costs incurred in respect of work done after the date of the costs capping order but excluding the amount of any additional liability. (2) This Section does not apply to judicial review costs capping orders under Part 4 of the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015 or to protective costs orders. (Rules 46.16 to 46.19 make provision for judicial review costs capping orders under Part 4 of the Criminal Justice and Courts Act 2015.)

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (3) Omitted. [PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (4) A costs capping order may be in respect of –

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (a) the whole litigation; or

[PART 3 – THE COURT’S CASE MANAGEMENT POWERS > 3.19] (b) any issues which are ordered to be tried separately.
